git.description: Distributed version control system, the de facto standard for software development.

npm.description: Node package manager, installed alongside Node.js.

python.description: General-purpose programming language widely used for scripting, data, and AI.

pip.description: Python package installer, installed alongside Python.

npmrc.description:
fund=false: disable funding prompts
audit=false: skip install audit, speed up installs
progress=false: disable progress bar
Reduce npm logs, cut down steps, and cut tokens fed to AI.

contains.desc: Disable install-time security audit to speed up installs
Hide the download progress bar to reduce log noise

rtk.description: A toolkit for reducing token consumption. rtk injects itself into the AI software context — prefixing each command with rtk filters or trims its input, cutting AI input-token usage.

pwsh.description: Microsoft's modern cross-platform shell — far more capable than CMD and the built-in Windows PowerShell, with better compatibility.

uv.description: Blazing-fast Python package and environment manager written in Rust; replaces pip / pipx / virtualenv and is a common dependency base for AI tooling.

ffmpeg.description: The Swiss-army knife of audio/video processing: transcoding, cutting, streaming and frame extraction — a dependency of many AI multimodal tools.

ripgrep.description: Extremely fast code search (a modern grep replacement); recursive and .gitignore-aware by default, a common dependency of AI coding assistants.

maple_fonts.description: Maple Mono monospace coding font (Nerd Font, CN edition): rounded design, strict 2:1 CJK width, built-in terminal icons and CJK glyphs — great for terminals and editors.
